methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi, has raised $30M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 private companies at Series C stage in the same sector—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—alongside 1 public comparable and 8 additional private peers in adjacent positions.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression, using total raised as a proxy base of $30M and applying a typical 1.9x Series B-to-next-stage multiplier, implies $57M. Peer-median triangulation across the 3-company cohort yields $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The spread reflects material variance in how far along the capital curve peers have progressed, though all operate in overlapping climate technology markets.

Triangulation across both methods produces a valuation range of $48M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $528M. The wide dispersion—more than a 20x span—reflects genuine uncertainty around stage-specific risk, technology maturity, and market timing in frontier energy sectors. The peer-median method dominates the upper bound given Cemvita's positioning alongside later-stage funded competitors. Key uncertainties include technology validation progress, capital efficiency relative to peers, and path-to-revenue visibility, all of which would narrow this range materially with additional diligence.
